resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Inspection (resale)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Highlands Department of Buildings & Housing (Housing Officer), inspected together with the Fire Prevention Division
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are not scheduled until payment is received. The combined housing and fire fee is lowest when the inspection is scheduled and paid more than 10 days ahead.
requirements: Before the inspection is scheduled, the Cashier checks with the Tax Search Officer that taxes and sewer fees are current, with the Technical Assistant for open construction (UCC) permits or violations, and with the Code Enforcement Officer for violations
Open permits or violations must be inspected and closed before the housing and fire inspections are scheduled; flood-plain homes are checked for substantial improvement

Housing inspection to the Borough's Property Maintenance Code (exterior property, sidewalks and driveways, exterior structure and paint, roofs, stairs, decks, handrails, windows that open and have screens, doors and locks, interior surfaces, plumbing, heating, electrical)
Smoke/carbon monoxide inspection by the Fire Prevention Division at the same time (see fire certificate)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Application for Residential Certificate of Inspection (checking "Sale of Property" or "Transfer of Title") and email it to the Cashier at cashier@highlandsnj.gov. Pay by check in person or by mail to Borough Hall, 151 Navesink Avenue, Highlands, NJ 07732 (one combined payment covers housing and fire). Then call the Housing Secretary at 732-872-1224 ext. 204 to schedule, and give access to the property.

evidence.quote: Schedule your inspection by calling the Housing Secretary at 732-872-1224, ext. 204.
INSPECTIONS WILL NOT BE SCHEDULED UNTIL PAYMENT IS RECEIVED
A certificate of inspection shall be required for any new rental, rerental, or sale of a space or property.
□ Rental/Lease of Space □ Transfer of Title □ Sale of Property
Cashier checks with Tax Search Officer to confirm taxes and sewer fees are current

resale_co.notes: Borough code Chapters 10 and 11 were read through the ecode360 print view (ecode360 code HI4100 is Highlands Borough, not Atlantic Highlands). Section 10-5.2 requires a certificate of inspection for any sale. The combined fee is the $100 housing fee plus the fire tier. The Borough page gives $145 / $190 / $261 (which matches $100 plus $45 / $90 / $161 in the code), while the application form (revised 07.01.2025) shows $225 for the 1 to 3 day tier; confirm which applies. The page also says fire tiers are "1-4 days" while the code says "Less than 4 business days". No validity period for a resale certificate was found. The workflow names Housing Officers Charlie Wells and Albert Souza, Code Enforcement Officer William Brunt and Cashier Tina Foster. The workflow quote is from a PDF whose text uses ligatures, so exact matching may need care. Short-term and long-term rental rules are rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19

Borough code (Section 11-10a4) says 1 and 2 family homes may not be sold unless hard-wired smoke detection devices are installed, with at least one per level and one within 15 feet of the main heating plant (a heat detector if the heating plant is in a confined space)
Fire extinguisher (form still lists it): the application and workflow still name a smoke/carbon detector and fire extinguisher certificate

authorities.how_to_apply: Use the same Borough Application for Residential Certificate of Inspection and Certificate of Smoke/Carbon Detector & Fire Extinguisher; one combined payment covers housing and fire. Email the form to cashier@highlandsnj.gov, pay by check at Borough Hall, and call 732-872-1224 ext. 204 to schedule.

fire_cert.notes: Fire tiers come from Borough code Section 11-8 (ecode360 print text runs the amount into the line, as quoted). The Borough's local amendment requiring hard-wired smoke detectors at sale (Section 11-10a4, 2019) is stricter than the state rule, which accepts 10-year sealed battery alarms in older homes; confirm what the inspector enforces. The Borough form and workflow still mention a fire extinguisher certificate, which P.L.2025, c.19 dropped from the state sale certificate in February 2025.

other_items.label: Taxes and sewer fees current
other_items.detail: Before scheduling the inspection, the Cashier confirms with the Tax Search Officer that property taxes and sewer fees are current.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: Open construction permits or code violations must be inspected and closed before the housing and fire inspections are scheduled; homes in the flood plain are checked for substantial improvement.

Is a fire extinguisher still checked after P.L.2025, c.19?
